agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The pass ran on the edited model. The per-text means shown cover whole prompts, so they're uninformative here. I'll extract the logprob of "Let" at the first answer position for each of the 512 dev_a prompts and compare with the original's choices from generation. For the damage subset, I'll compare answer-token logprobs (prompt excluded) with the original's fwd_3 values for the same 500 texts: loop copy and novel tokens, controls, own-correct answers and references. Confirmation means a much higher share of prompts with P(Let) > 0.5 and small damage.

Edit S(1.0) works mechanically. The probability of opening with "Let" now exceeds 0.5 for 96% of prompts, up from 51%: prompts that originally chose markdown now give "Let" a mean probability of 0.85. Collateral change is small: own-correct answers fall by 0.003 nats per token, controls by 0.004, references by 0.02, and copied loop tokens are unchanged. Now the real test is whether switching mode improves accuracy. I'll run a paired "both" generation on 256 problems from dev_b, which was not used to compute the style direction. Within-stratum differences predict a gain of roughly 4-5 points, since about half the answers switch mode and those gain about 9 points. A gain near or above +3 would support the hypothesis. No change, or a loss (for example through more plain-mode loops), would refute it.

The S(1.0) edit is backed up in /work/best_S1. Now the paired generation test on 256 dev_b problems. In the same pass, it compares the original with edit S(1.0), which amplifies the layer 16-19 plain-mode write.

Switching mode gave only +1.6 ± 2.4 points (21 wrong→right, 17 right→wrong). The cause is visible in the cut share: it rose from 28.5% to 36.7%, because plain mode loops more often. So the plain mode's better reasoning is partly cancelled by its higher looping rate, consistent with the stratified table (plain cut 23-40% vs markdown 14-27%). I'll check the edited answers: style share, accuracy among finished answers by style, and whether the new cut-offs are the same line-repetition loops. If finished plain answers are clearly more accurate but loops eat the gain, the next step is to pair the mode switch with a loop-specific fix rather than abandon it.
